title: Prince Creek Formation, Alaska: polar dinosaurs
summary: About 69 million years ago the Prince Creek Formation was an Arctic floodplain on Alaska's North Slope, and its rocks hold the richest known record of polar dinosaurs. They include the hadrosaur Ugrunaaluk kuukpikensis, which roamed in herds and is known mostly from the Liscomb Bone Bed on the Colville River, and the horned Pachyrhinosaurus perotorum, in a land of months-long winter darkness and probable snow.

uncertainty.note: Sources give about 69 million years ago for the formation and 70–69 Ma for P. perotorum.

as_recorded.value: a unit of rock deposited on the Arctic flood plain about 69 million years ago
P. perotorum is the youngest centrosaurine known (70–69 Ma)

importance.justification: Preserves the northernmost known Cretaceous dinosaur communities, which lived through polar winters.
